contents.name: Realification and the real basis induced by a finite complex basis
contents.locator: Section 2.1, Linear algebra, PDF p. 5 (journal p. 88)
contents.support: The article states that restriction of scalars makes a complex linear space a real linear space and that a finite complex basis f1,...,fn gives the real basis f1,if1,...,fn,ifn. The local proof checks the exact supplied-list and zero-dimensional cases and adds the normed-subspace metric conclusion.

contents.name: Definition 1.1: real/complex norm axioms and induced norm metric
contents.support: Step 1.1 checks the complex line is a subspace with restricted norm; step 2.1 invokes the A lemma for the identical restricted real metric. The metric restriction is proved locally, rather than attributed as a separate theorem to the notes.

contents.name: Example 1.2(1): finite-dimensional coordinate p-norms over R or C
contents.support: The example norm N(z1,z2)=|z1|+|z2| is exactly the K=C,n=2,p=1 specialization. The local supplier lem-complex-coordinate-l1-is-a-norm proves the norm claim. Kochanek does not choose the subspace C(1,i) or state its displayed real basis.
